mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases for three consecutive monthly observations
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and suppresses earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO contraction below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month MA
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 10% from the prior month signals a collapse in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST falls by more than 10% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the unemployment rate and payroll employment (PAYEMS) at a decelerating pace (PAYEMS growth < 0.2% while UNRATE > 4.5%) signals labor market softening, which reduces consumer purchasing power and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 4.5% and PAYEMS growth < 0.2% simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 5-year average, combined with a concurrent drop in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals a reduction in household financial buffers and spending power, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 5-year average and GDPC1 YoY growth < 0
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is below its 5-year average and GDPC1 is flat or declining year-over-year.
